rows.speaker: شهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: A man who insisted on looking into the cave emerged with whitened eyes and changed hair, and said the sleepers numbered seven; the report could support their present existence.
rows.anchor: عن شهر بن حوشب قال : كان لي صاحب ماض شديد النفس فمر بجانب الكهف

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli transmits that some people held the sleepers still existed in the cave.
rows.anchor: فحكى السهيلي عن قوم القول به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas denied their bones remained, saying they had disappeared more than three hundred years earlier when he passed the cave with Habib b. Maslama; the report is from Ikrima.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة أن ابن عباس غزا مع حبيب بن مسلمة فمروا بالكهف فإذا فيه عظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi inclines to their no longer existing and, when alive, not remaining in the described state; the verse reports their condition then and addresses no particular individual.
rows.anchor: والذي يميل القلب إليه عدم وجودهم اليوم وإنهم كانوا موجودين فليسوا على تلك الحالة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed through Ibn Mardawayh to Ibn Abbas says the Prophet called the Companions of the Cave helpers of the Mahdi; even if sound, it does not prove they exist today in that state.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : أصحاب الكهف أعوان المهدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Prophet is treated as specifically addressed, the flight-and-terror consequence is explained by ordinary human nature; another proposal distinguishes God's disclosure to him from an unaided personal sighting.
rows.anchor: ومن جعله صلى الله عليه وسلم معينا قال : المراد لو اطلعت عليهم لوليت منهم فرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An anecdote about Moses teaches that the first cure worked because he went to the plant through God, while the later attempt relied on himself.
rows.anchor: السبب أنك في المرة الأولى ذهبت منا إلى النبات وفي المرة الثانية ذهبت من نفسك إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi calls it objectionable for a mystic to claim he would not flee or feel terror if he saw the sleepers.
rows.anchor: ومما يستهجن من القول ما يحكى عن بعض المتصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The excuse that the speaker meant he was like an unafraid child does not remove the impropriety; Alusi likens it to an irreverent claim about God's knowledge of the unseen and invokes Umar's advice to speak understandably.
rows.anchor: لا يدفع الاستهجان وذلك نظير قول من قال سبحانه وتعالى لا يعلم الغيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، الحرميان، أبو حيوة، ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: These readers intensify the lām and retain the hamza in ولملئت.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحرميان وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة ( ولملئت ) بتشديد اللام والهمزة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، شيبة
rows.claim: They intensify the lām and change the hamza to yāʾ in the reading of ولملئت.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة بتشديد اللام وقلب الهمزة ياء

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri reads with a light lām and the hamza changed to yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري بالتخفيف والقلب

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر، عيسى
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and ʿIsa read ruʿuban with ḍamma on the ʿayn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعيسى ( رعبا ) بضم العين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their awakening is likened to their prolonged sleep; the correspondence is that both are signs of God's overwhelming power.
rows.anchor: فالمشبه الإيقاظ والشبه به الإنامة المشار إليها ووجه الشبه كون كل منهما ءاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose or consequence of awakening them was that they question one another, leading to the wisdoms narrated next; mentioning this effect also entails the other effects.
rows.anchor: أي ليسأل بعضهم بعضا فيترتب عليه ما فصل من الحكم البالغة

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji favors reading the lām as consequential: questioning was an outcome, since God's purpose was to display His power rather than to cause their discussion.
rows.anchor: وجعل غير واحد اللام للعاقبة واستظهره الخفاجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dialogue's introductory قال is a resumption that explains how they questioned one another.
rows.anchor: ﴿ قال ﴾ ( استئناف لبيان تساؤلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner is identified either as their leader Maksalmina or as Yamlikha, who managed their provisions.
rows.anchor: قيل هو كبيرهم مكسلمينا وقيل صاحب نفقتهم يمليخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questioner may have remarked on the unusual mismatch between their condition and what normally happens; another suggestion is that they were alarmed at missing prayer.
rows.anchor: لما رأى من مخالفة حالهم لما هو المعتاد في الجملة

rows.speaker: غير واحد
rows.claim: They used aw for uncertainty because they could not establish how long they had slept; Alusi says sleep haze kept them from checking signs, whatever the time of sleep or waking.
rows.anchor: أو للشك كما قاله غير واحد والمراد لم نتحقق مقدار لبثنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The well-known account has them sleep in the morning and wake late in the day; another says they could not tell whether it was the same or next day.
rows.anchor: والمشهور أن نومهم كان غدوة وانتباههم كان آخر النهار وقيل فلم يدروا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes aw as a correction: they first said a day, then noticed the sun had not set and corrected it to part of a day; Alusi maintains the straightforward reading is doubt.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا قيل إن أو للإضراب وذلك أنهم لما انتبهوا آخر النهار

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports a distributive reading: some said a day and others part of a day, each speaking from probable judgment; Alusi says this reading is unlikely and conjecture is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو حيان أنها للتفصيل على معنى قال بعضهم : لبثنا يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply that God knows their stay best gently corrects the first group, displays proper etiquette, and marks the dialogue's two groups; the same speaker saying both is disfavored by the discourse structure.
rows.anchor: وهذا رد منهم على الأولين على أحسن ما يكون من مراعاة حسن الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that one person made both statements does not fit the passage's resumption and question-and-answer form.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا يساعده النظم الكريم فإن الاستئناف في الحكاية والخطاب في المحكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥadukum means one of you; using aḥad rather than wāḥid avoids a possible implication that they mean their chief.
rows.anchor: أي واحدا منكم ولم يقل واحدكم لإيهامه إرادة سيدكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wariq is commonly explained as minted dirhams, though another view includes unminted silver; the Arfaja report about a silver nose that became foul supports the broader sense, while al-Asmaʿi's paper-leaf reading is dismissed because the report of silver rotting is unsound.
rows.anchor: أي بدراهمكم المضروبة كما هو مشهور بين اللغويين وقيل الورق الفضة مضروبة أو غير مضروبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reciters vary on wariqikum: many use a still rāʾ, Abu Rajaʾ and others use kasra on wāw with assimilation, a form with kasra on rāʾ is defended as rare Arabic, al-Zajjaj reports a non-assimilated form, and ʿAli reads bawariqikum as a collective noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة وأبو بكر والحسن والأعمش واليزيدي ويعقوب في رواية وخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the coin hadhihi suggests the speaker held it out; carrying provisions for livelihood is compatible with reliance on God, as the saying instructs one to tie the camel and trust.
rows.anchor: وفي حملهم دليل على التأهب لأسباب المعاش لمن خرج من منزله بحمل النفقة

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Some eminent scholars define the elect's trust as abandoning all causes, citing Khalid's drinking poison and reports of Saʿd, Abu Muslim, and Tamim facing extraordinary dangers.
rows.anchor: إن توكل الخواص ترك الأسباب بالكلية

rows.speaker: أحمد، إسحق
rows.claim: Ahmad, Ishaq, and other imams allow those strong in certainty and reliance to cross deserts without provisions and to forgo earning or medical treatment; Ahmad defines trust as ending dependence on people.
rows.anchor: وقد نص الإمام أحمد وإسحق وغيرهما من الأئمة على جواز دخول المفاوز بغير زاد

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: The account of Abraham refusing Gabriel's offer of help while being thrown into the fire illustrates reliance directly on God.
rows.anchor: واستدل عليه بقول إبراهيم عليه السلام حين عرض له جبريل عليه السلام يوم ألقي في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The position that abandoning means of support is uniquely a Sufi doctrine is mistaken; it is also reported from others.
rows.anchor: بل جاء عن غيرهم أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city was their familiar home city, reportedly called Ephesus when they left and later Tarsus; this reconciles the two transmitted names.
rows.anchor: وهي المدينة التي خرجوا منها قيل وتسمى الآن طرطوس وكان اسمها يوم خرجوا منها أفسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their immediate turn to obtaining food instead of investigating their situation exemplifies a wise redirection to what mattered then; the verse's fa also signals this.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا القول صدر منهم إعراضا عن التعمق في البحث وإقبالا على ما يهمهم بحسب الحال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people of the city sacrificed to idols; another report says they sacrificed pigs, so azka can mean lawful.
rows.anchor: فإن أهل المدينة كانوا في عهدهم يذبحون للطواغيت كما روى سعيد بن منصور

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says most of the townspeople's wealth had been usurped, supporting a request for the purest lawful food.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك : إن أكثر أموالهم كانت مغصوبة

rows.speaker: ابن السائب، مقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saʾib and Muqatil explain azka as more wholesome or pleasant; if it means lawful, it returns to the preceding interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن السائب ومقاتل : أي أطيب

rows.speaker: عكرمة، يمان بن ريان
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says azka means more plentiful, while Yaman b. Rayyan says cheaper.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة : أي أكثر وقال يمان بن ريان : أي أرخص

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets azka as best quality, which Alusi calls the best reading; it may also mean rice, dates, or raisins, though the youths are presumed to seek lawful food.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة : أي أجود وهو أجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The increase implied by zakāh can be spiritual and otherworldly, as in the reward and good outcome of seeking lawful food, or material and worldly, as in abundance, affordability, or quality.
rows.anchor: وأصلها النمو والزيادة وهي تكون معنوية أخروية وحسية دنيوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ay may be an interrogative subject with azka as predicate, or a relative object with an elided predicate; its suffix can refer to the city, its people, or the food understood from context.
rows.anchor: وأي استفهام مبتدأ و ( أزكى ) خبره والجملة معلق عنها الفعل للاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in rizqan minhu may refer to the best food or to the coins, making min partitive, source-marking, or a substitute marker; in either case the requested provision should be lawful.
rows.anchor: أي من ذلك الأزكى طعاما فمن لابتداء الغاية أو التبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to act gently means either to treat people tactfully so no quarrel exposes them, to hide their entry and exit, or to avoid being cheated; the next command warns not to let anyone in town notice them.
rows.anchor: اللطف في المعاملة كيلا تقع خصومة تجر إلى معرفته أو ليتكلف اللطف في الاستخفاء دخولا وخروجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the concealment interpretations, wa-la-yushʿirannakum confirms and explains tact; the Imam takes it literally as do not inform anyone about you.
rows.anchor: وفسره الإمام بلا يخبرن بكم أحدا فهو على ظاهره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the imperative lām in yatalattaf with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( وليتلطف ) بكسر لام الأمر

rows.speaker: قتيبة الميال
rows.claim: Qutayba al-Mayyāl reads yutalattaf with a passive verb and ḍamma on yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وعن قتيبة الميال ( وليتلطف ) بضم الياء مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: قتيبة، أبو صالح، يزيد بن القعقاع
rows.claim: They read yushʿirannakum as an active verb and aḥad as its nominative subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هو وأبو صالح ويزيد بن القعقاع ( ولا يشعرن بكم أحد ) ببناء الفعل للفاعل ورفع أحد

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi calls the passage the strongest proof for agency; al-Kiya also derives the permissibility of pooling group coins, jointly buying and sharing food, with an eater allowed extra money for his portion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي : وهي أقوىءاية في ذلك وفيها كما قال الكيا دليل على جواز خلط دراهم الجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths sent one of their number, identified by many as Yamlikha; God caused them to be discovered just as He had put them to sleep and awakened them.
rows.anchor: وكان على ما قال غير واحد يمليخا فكان ما أشار الله تعالى إليه بقوله سبحانه ( وكذلك أعثرنا عليهم

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam takes the demonstrative to refer specifically to their awakening after the long sleep.
rows.anchor: وقال العز بن عبد السلام في أماليه : الإشارة إلى البعث المخصوص

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Raghib gives the original meaning of ʿathara as falling face-first and cites proverbs about a generous horse rarely stumbling and the safe well-trodden road.
rows.anchor: وأصل العثور كما قال الراغب السقوط للوجه

rows.speaker: المطرزي
rows.claim: Al-Mutarrizi explains discovery as a metaphor from stumbling: a fallen person looks at where he fell, so the word came to mean finding out, by a familiar causal relation.
rows.anchor: لما كان كل عاثر ينظر إلى موضع عثرته ورد العثور بمعنى الاطلاع والعرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first object of aʿtharnā is omitted to make it general: God let people discover the youths.
rows.anchor: ومفعول ( أعثرنا ) الأول محذوف لقصد العموم أي وكذلك أطلعنا الناس عليهم

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the people who learned as the townspeople who saw the youths' extraordinary condition; God's promise means the resurrection promise or what He promised, namely resurrection, is true and certain.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : أهل مدينتهم ( ليعلموا ( أي الذين أطلعناهم عليهم بما عاينوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour is the time when all creatures are raised for judgment and recompense; witnessing the youths' extraordinary death-like sleep and awakening defeats reliance on improbability as a reason to doubt it.
rows.anchor: القيامة التي هي في لسان الشرع عبارة عن وقت بعث الخلائق جميعا للحساب والجزاء

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A scholar argues that seeing God preserve the youths' souls and bodies for over three hundred years and return their souls proves He can resurrect, judge, and reward the dead.
rows.anchor: إن من شاهد أنه جل وعلا توفى نفوسهم وأمسكها ثلثمائة سنة وأكثر حافظا أبدانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi questions whether the episode establishes judgment and recompense; an objection says preserving bodies is unlike reassembling scattered parts, and he finds the reply from intuitive inference worth considering but not decisive.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن في استفادة العلم بالمحاسبة والمجازاة من الاطلاع على حال القوم نظرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers explaining the inference from the youths' preserved bodies, suspended senses, and restoration after centuries: an event as extraordinary as resurrection removes the doubt that arises from finding resurrection improbable.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأظهر توجيه الترتب بما ذكره أولا وتوضيحه أن حال الفتية حيث ناموا في تلك المدة المديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event directly establishes resurrection's possibility, not certainty that it will happen; certainty of fulfillment comes from the truthful report, while the event supplies a final part of the proof for those who heard it.
rows.anchor: فإن الظاهر أن العلم المذكور إنما يترتب على إخبار الصادق بوقوعه وعلى إمكانه في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes God's promise cover all He promised and the Hour a specification after that general statement; Alusi accepts it as a possible reading but disputes calling it the obvious one.
rows.anchor: بأن كل ما وعده سبحانه متحقق ويجعل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The temporal phrase idh yatanaazaʿun most naturally modifies aʿtharnā, placed first to emphasize the purpose; Abu Hayyan and Abu al-Baqa also attach it to liyaʿlamu, though Alusi raises objections.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان وأبو البقاء وغيرهما كونه ظرفا ( ليعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanaazuʿ originally means pulling against one another and figuratively means disputing; it takes a direct object in its literal sense but fi with the sense of quarrel.
rows.anchor: وأصل التنازع التجاذب ويعبر به عن التخاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute is about resurrection: people differed between affirming it, denying it, raising souls alone, or raising both souls and bodies, the last being the Muslim doctrine.
rows.anchor: فمن مقر به وجاحد وقائل يقول تبعث الأرواح دون الأجساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrative says a later believing king, faced with disagreement over resurrection, prayed for a sign; a shepherd opened the cave, the youths awoke, their old coins exposed their story, and after meeting the king they died, were placed in wooden coffins, and a mosque was built.
rows.anchor: روي أنه بعد أن ضرب الله تعالى على آذان الفتية ومضى دهر طويل لم يبق أحد من أمتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative report says the king matched the youth's names to an old tablet, then the youth entered first to spare his companions fear; God took their souls and obscured their traces, and the townspeople built a mosque after trusting the youth's account.
rows.anchor: وكان الملك قد سمع أن فتية قد فقدوا في الزمان الأول وإن أسماءهم مكتوبة على لوح في الخزانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes their affair the story of their former ordeal under the tyrant, which people had heard as legend without knowing whether the youths survived.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ضمير ( أمرهم ) للفتية والمراد بالأمر الشأن والحال الذي كان قبل الإعثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, the fa before build is an abbreviated transition: the purpose of discovery was achieved, the youths died, and the people then proposed a structure at the cave entrance.
rows.anchor: بناء على القول الأول فصيحة بلا ريب على أدب اختصارات القرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب، أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Bunyanan is parsed either as a singular noun with no plural, a plural of bunyana, or a cognate accusative; the builders sought to protect the youths' resting place from intrusion.
rows.anchor: نصب على أنه مفعول به وهو كما قال الراغب وأحد لا جمع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabbuhum aʿlam bihim may be the finders submitting knowledge of lineage, condition, and duration to God, or God's rebuke to those speculating, including the finders or the People of the Book in the Prophet's time.
rows.anchor: أن يكون من كلام المتنازعين المعثرين كأنهم تذاكروا أمرهم وتناقلوا الكلام في أنسابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some assign amrahum to the youths and read the dispute as what to do after their death, how to honor them, or uncertainty whether they had died or merely slept again.
rows.anchor: تدبير أمرهم وحالهم حين توفوا كيف يفعلون بهم وبماذا يجلون قدرهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari offers further options: amrahum may concern the finders' religion and resurrection, the people's discussion of the cave youths' story, or plans to conceal the youths' location after death.
rows.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري احتمال كون الضمير ( أمرهم ) للمعثرين وإن المراد من أمرهم أمر دينهم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشف
rows.claim: The author of al-Kashf distinguishes the conjunction: the fa is explanatory in one account and consecutive in the others, including when people stop discussing the story and turn to the practical matter of building.
rows.anchor: وذكر صاحب الكشف أن الفاء على الأول فصيحة لا محال وعلى الآخرين للتعقيب

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan allows the pronoun in liyaʿlamu to refer to the youths, with their discovery increasing their knowledge; the dispute then begins a new account about the townspeople and their building plans.
rows.anchor: وحكى في البحر أن ضمير ( ليعلموا ) عائد على أصحاب الكهف والمراد أعثرنا عليهم ليزدادوا علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says this reading is not far-fetched if one sets aside external reports, though he knows of no commentator who takes all the pronouns as referring to the youths and idh as modifying discovery.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن جعل ذلك الضمير للفتية وإن دعا لتأويل يعلم بما سمعت ليس ببعيد الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi considers it remote that rabbuhum aʿlam is God's speech rebuking the disputants, and very remote to assign all pronouns to the youths; its apparent sense is the finders' response to uncertainty over life and death.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه حكاية عن المعثرين وهو شديد الملاءمة جدا لكون التنازع في أمرهم من الموت والحياة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada, in reports from ʿAbd al-Razzaq and Ibn Abi Hatim, identifies those who prevailed as the rulers; their first-person oath to build suits people with authority.
rows.anchor: كما أخرج عبد الرزاق وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة الولاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others identify the prevailing group as the Muslim king, the youths' relatives, or town leaders; Alusi finds the first identification too narrow in number and the relatives implausible without surviving kin, while many say the king and Muslims.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذين غلبوا قيل الملك المسلم وقيل أولياء أصحاب الكهف وقيل رؤساء البلد

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj infers that believers in resurrection prevailed because mosques are established by believers.
rows.anchor: وعن الزجاج أن هذا يدل على أنه لما ظهر أمرهم غلب المؤمنون بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the first group were unbelievers seeking a church or pagan sanctuary, while believers opposed them and built a mosque; another report says the king built a church with an inscription, suggesting mosque here names the Christian community's place of worship.
rows.anchor: بناء بيعة أو مصنع لكفرهم فمانعهم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the king planned a mosque beside the righteous youths where he could worship God until death.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو حاتم عن السدي أن الملك قال : لأتخذن عند هؤلاء القوم الصالحين مسجدا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the mosque was for the youths to pray in upon waking; this assumes they remained asleep, a view extended by some to say they await the Mahdi, which Alusi dismisses as fables.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه اتخذ ليصلي فيه أصحاب الكهف إذا استيقظوا وهذا مبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the first group were unbelievers, not every finder shared the resurrection lesson; they may have wished to seal the cave because they did not know the youths had slept and awakened.
rows.anchor: ولعل تلك الطائفة لم تتحقق حالهم وأنهم ناموا تلك المدة ثم بعثوا

rows.speaker: الحسن، عيسى الثقفي
rows.claim: They read ghulibū in the passive: believing finders who opposed construction were overpowered and yielded that, if anything were built, it should be a mosque.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى الثقفي ( غلبوا ) بضم الغين وكسر اللام على أن الفعل مبني للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects using the verse to permit building mosques over righteous graves or praying there, despite al-Khafaji's claim; he cites multiple prophetic reports cursing grave-visitors who make mosques and lamps at graves and those who turn prophets' graves into mosques.
rows.anchor: واستدل بالآية على جواز البناء على قبور الصلحاء واتخاذ مسجد عليها وجواز الصلاة في ذلك

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Reports from Ibn Abbas, Aisha, Abu Hurayra, and others condemn turning prophets' graves into mosques; another says people who build over a righteous person's grave and place images there are among the worst at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لعن الله تعالى زائرات القبور والمتخذين عليها المساجد والسرج

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Other reports call grave-mosque makers among the worst people and say God cursed earlier Israelites for making graves into mosques.
rows.anchor: إن من شرار الناس من تدركهم الساعة وهم أحياء ومن يتخذ القبور مساجد

rows.speaker: ابن حجر
rows.claim: Ibn Hajar lists making graves into mosques, praying toward them, touching them, and circumambulating them among major sins; Alusi explains a mosque means praying on or toward a grave, especially one revered as a prophet's or saint's.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن حجر في الزواجر أنه وقع في كلام بعض الشافعية عند اتخاذ القبور مساجد

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Shafiʿi jurists prohibit prayer toward prophets' and saints' graves for blessing or veneration, requiring both a revered grave and intent to pray toward it; the same logic can extend to lamps and circumambulation as acts of veneration.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم قال أصحابنا : تحرم الصلاة إلى قبور الأنبياء والأولياء تبركا وإعظاما

rows.speaker: بعض الحنابلة
rows.claim: Some Hanbalis call prayer at a grave for blessing defiance of God and His Messenger, an unauthorized innovation, and a major cause of shirk; they require demolishing grave structures and removing lamps.
rows.anchor: قصد الرجل الصلاة عند القبر متبركا به عين المحاداة لله تعالى ورسوله

rows.speaker: المنهاج وشرحه
rows.claim: The Minhaj and its commentary disfavor plastering graves and building around them outside endowed cemeteries, except where protection is needed, and prohibit construction in endowed cemeteries; grave inscriptions are also generally disfavored.
rows.anchor: ويكره تجصيص القبر والبناء عليه في حريمه وخارجه في غير المسبلة

rows.speaker: الأذرعي
rows.claim: Al-Adhraʿi argues that writing Quran on graves is forbidden because it risks disrespect through trampling, impurity, and rain; writing a name merely to identify a grave is recommended by some.
rows.anchor: نعم بحث الأذرعي حرمة كتابة القرآن لتعريضه للامتهان بالدوس والتنجيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi rejects an appeal to widespread grave inscriptions as consensus: visible grave construction is even more common despite known prohibition, the practice was not universal, and any practical consensus presupposes eras when moral correction can be enforced.
rows.anchor: ويرد بمنع هذه الكلية وبفرضها فالبناء على قبورهم أكثر من الكتابة عليها

rows.speaker: ابن الرفعة
rows.claim: The quoted legal discussion says structures over graves in public burial grounds must be demolished, including domes, unless harm is feared, in which case the matter goes to the ruler.
rows.anchor: وينبغي لكل أحد هدم ذلك ما لم يخش منه مفسدة فيتعين الرفع للإمام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In Sahih Muslim, Ali says the Prophet sent him to erase every image and level every raised grave; Ibn al-Humam limits this to high, decorated structures built over graves.
rows.anchor: أن لا تدع تمثالا إلا طمسته ولا قبرا مشرفا إلا سويته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier-law arguments by Muhammad, Abu Yusuf, and al-Karkhi do not establish mosque-building on graves: earlier law binds only when recounted without condemnation, whereas the Prophet cursed those who did this.
rows.anchor: مذهبنا في شرع من قبلنا وإن كان إنه يلزمنا على أن شريعتنا لكن لا مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument that this verse legislates a rule inherited from earlier communities fails: unlike explicit precedents used by jurists, it merely narrates a group's statement and intention without praising or endorsing their action.
rows.anchor: ليس فيها أكثر من حكاية قول طائفة من الناس وعزمهم على فعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the verse neither identifies an infallible group nor praises its plan, neither their action nor intention proves that grave mosques are lawful.
rows.anchor: فمتى لم يثبت أن فيهم معصوما لا يدل فعلهم فضلا عن عزمهم على مشروعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the account that rulers prevailed, the first group may have been believers who wanted only to build at the cave entrance and close it; they did not bury the youths because death was uncertain and awe prevented entry.
rows.anchor: إن الطائفة الأولى كانوا مؤمنين عالمين بعدم مشروعية اتخاذ المساجد على القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the second group is viewed favorably, their mosque may have stood near the cave or over the cave on the mountain rather than over the bodies, as reports from al-Suddi, Wahb, and Mujahid indicate.
rows.anchor: فلك أن تقول : إن اتخاذهم المسجد عليهم ليس على طرز اتخاذ المساجد على القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the verse to defend grave veneration, plastered structures, hanging lamps, prayer toward graves, circumambulation, touching, or scheduled gatherings opposes God and His Messenger and invents an unauthorized religion.
rows.anchor: محتجا بهذه الآية الكريمة وبما جاء في بعض روايات القصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To know the right practice, examine how the Prophet's companions treated his grave, the finest grave on earth, when visiting and greeting him.
rows.anchor: ويكفيك في معرفة الحق تتبع ما صنع أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قبره

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya reports a cave near Loja in Granada with bodies and a dog's remains, said locally to be the cave youths; he visited it in 504 AH and saw a nearby Roman ruin called al-Raqim.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية دخلت عليهم فرأيتهم سنة أربع وخمسمائة وهم بهذه الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says Andalusi visitors claimed the occupants were hard to count and accompanied by a dog, and he personally saw large stones in the nearby ruins; he considered Andalusia likely because Christianity was dominant there and news from distant Arabia would be unlikely without revelation.
rows.anchor: وحين كنا بالأندلس كان الناس يزورون هذا الكهف ويذكرون أنهم يغلطون في عدتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports about Ibn Abbas and Muʿawiya weaken the preference for Andalusia, since Muʿawiya never entered it; Andalusi Christians being called Romans does not help, and many locate the cave at Tarsus.
rows.anchor: وما تقدم من خبر ابن عباس ومعاوية يضعف ما ادعى ترجحه لأن معاوية لم يدخل الأندلس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers promising to do anything one resolves in the future; ghadan primarily means the next day but the active participle already conveys futurity, which the phrase reinforces.
rows.anchor: أي فيما يستقبل من الزمان مطلقا وهو تأكيد لما يدل عليه اسم الفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: The occasion was Quraysh asking the Prophet about the Spirit, the Companions of the Cave, and Dhul-Qarnayn; he said he would answer the next day without qualifying the promise, and revelation was delayed fifteen days, with other reports giving three or forty.
rows.anchor: فإن الآية نزلت حين سألت قريش النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الروح وأصحاب الكهف وذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some limit the wording to the literal next day and derive broader future promises by implication; Alusi rejects the objection that later periods differ because obstacles can fade, since death is an obstacle and its possibility increases over time.
rows.anchor: وليس بشيء لأن المانع شامل للموت واحتمال في الزمان الواسع أقوى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya, following al-Tabari's rebuttal, calls the exception for God's will corrupt; Alusi says this is unfair and the exception properly attaches to the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقول ابن عطية اغترارا برد الطبري أنه من الفساد بحيث كان الواجب أن لا يحكى خروج عن الإنصاف

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: The exception can mean do not say it in any state except while mentioning God's will, since a spoken promise cannot literally be joined to the divine will; another analysis makes it a state exception with an elided bāʾ.
rows.anchor: إن التباس القول بحقيقة المشيئة محال فبقي أن يكون بذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may instead refer to times, with God's will interpreted as permission: do not speak until God authorizes it; it may also be a disconnected exception signaling a permanent prohibition because the time of God's will is unknown.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المستثنى من أعم الأوقات أي لا تقولن ذلك في وقت من الأوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permanent-prohibition reading is not that God never wills the Prophet to speak because such speech is intrinsically bad; limiting the rule to revelation still does not follow from the text's indefinite noun under negation.
rows.anchor: لأن القبح فيما نحن فيه على إطلاقه غير مسلم والتخصيص بما يتعلق بالوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading attaches the exception to the prohibition, and the Prophet's community is included in the address; it cannot sensibly attach to the declaration that he will act, because either proposed sense conflicts with the prohibition.
rows.anchor: الظاهر في الآية الوجه الأول
